newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia police fire teargas at rioting students.
newsitem.headline: Zambia police fire teargas at rioting students.

text.p: Zambia police fired teargas and used batons to break up student riots at the University of Zambia on Monday, witnesses said.
They said several students were arrested after they vandalised university property and stoned vehicles on the campus in several hours of looting on Sunday night.
Riot police were sent to the campus on Monday and fought pitched battles with scores of stone-throwing students, finally driving them back with teargas.
"We understand several students were arrested, but we do not yet know how many," university spokesman Mulife Malambo told Reuters.
Malambo said students were unhappy over delays in the disbursement of book allowances.
"We have told the students that the university is not responsible for their allowances. The government is," Malambo said.
"However, the students have decided to call for a class boycott and the normal schedule has been disrupted," he added.
Last November the university was closed for several weeks due to student riots sparked by a protest over the way general elections, boycotted by seven opposition parties, had been organised.
President Frederick Chiluba's Movement for Multi-party Democracy won the November election, but the poll results were dismissed by international observers as flawed.
Students at Zambia's second university on Monday urged the government to pay meal and food allowances which they said were two weeks overdue.
"Students are starving and their morale to go to classes is very low. Government should immediately pay us the money," a student leader at the Copperbelt University said.
